old.name: Line
old.label: No.1 EUROPE 2026
old.teaser: Europe's No.1 bar by the 2026 vote — house-fermented fruit 'Why-ins' poured in a Kato Petralona ex-gallery.
old.text: Opened 2022 inside a former art gallery and run on circularity — the team ferments its own fruit wines (the cloudy, live 'Why-ins', made with winemaker Thanos Georgilas), brews its own beer and bakes sourdough, so almost nothing leaves the room as waste. Founders Vasilis Kyritsis and Nikos Bakoulis — Greek World Class champions of 2012 and 2011, the pair behind The Clumsies — took it to Europe's No.1 within four years, crowned at the Amsterdam ceremony on 30 June 2026. Not central and with no Acropolis view: a fermentation-first room on a Kato Petralona backstreet, ten minutes by taxi from Syntagma.
extra: Pour: a Why-in (Classic or Fancy), or the Delusional Margarita — reposado tequila, mustard, ketchup, potato water, improbably clean.

old.name: The Bar in Front of the Bar
old.label: No.2 EUROPE 2026
old.teaser: A pop-up built to hide renovation scaffolding became Europe's No.2 bar — eight zero-waste drinks rewritten every single day.
old.text: It began as a pavement pop-up of a few stools, thrown up to hide the building works on the 'real' bar the trio were opening behind it — and the decoy out-famed the original. Alexandros Tselepis, Konstantinos Theodorakopoulos and Symeon Papanikolaou now rewrite eight zero-waste cocktails every single day from the prep leftovers of Rumble in the Jungle, the jungle-themed room hidden behind the scaffold; the LED sign ('We serve humans too') became a Petraki landmark. No roof and no indoor seat: in rain or a February wind it is simply not the same bar.
extra: Pour: today's board of eight — zero-waste, classical bones, bright seasonal Greek fruit; let the team choose.

old.name: Baba au Rum
old.label: LEGEND OF THE LIST '25
old.teaser: Sixteen years on, the 2025 Legend of the List still re-earns its world ranking every year — no Athens bar has stayed this good this long.
old.text: Thanos Prunarus opened this 'rum and cocktail society' in 2009 on then-sleepy Klitiou lane, a full bar-generation before the city's 50 Best wave, and Greek press credits it as the cornerstone the modern Athens scene grew from. Four hundred-odd rums line the back bar of a small 1960s-pop room that spills onto the lane. In November 2025 the World's 50 Best organisation handed it the Rémy Martin Legend of the List award — the long-service honour — on its eleventh consecutive year in the ranking; it sits No.14 in Europe for 2026.
extra: Pour: the Supremus No.58 — rum, falernum, cold tea and ripe summer fruit, silky and deep — or a guided neat pour from the 400-bottle back bar.

bars:The Clumsies.group: Where it started, and the agave room

old.name: The Clumsies
old.label: SINCE 2014
old.teaser: The bar that put Athens on the world map, slipped to Europe's No.30 — still the city's grand all-day cocktail house.
old.text: Founded 2014 in the depths of the Greek recession, when Nikos Bakoulis and Vasilis Kyritsis — Greek World Class winners of 2011 and 2012 — talked three local businessmen into backing the transformation of a deteriorating Praxitelous building into an 'all-day bar'. It debuted at No.22 in 2015 and ran five straight world top-10 finishes to 2020, peaking at No.3; its founders then opened Line, which in 2026 took the European No.1 this first bar never quite reached. Three floors, coffee from morning to cocktails past midnight, and menus you can read only under UV light — no longer the insider find of 2017, but still the grand all-day cocktail house.
extra: Pour: the Mediterranean Gimlet — gin over a slow Greek-salad cordial of tomato water, cucumber, olive and oregano.

bars:Barro Negro.group: Where it started, and the agave room

old.name: Barro Negro
old.label: No.13 EUROPE 2026
old.teaser: Europe's No.13 bar is a Greek mezcaleria — the continent's agave conversation now runs through Klafthmonos Square.
old.text: Two Greeks who fell for Mexican agave opened the country's first agaveria in 2019 and named it for the black Oaxacan clay of a mezcal copita. Stelios Papadopoulos and George Kavaklis pour guided flights across the agave map — smoke, wet clay, green agave, citrus — from a list Greece did not have before them, and run the Academia de Barro Negro to teach Greek bartenders tequila and mezcal 'beyond shots', a January 2025 study trip to Mexico included. From forty-odd square metres on the edge of Klafthmonos Square to Europe's No.13 in seven years, with five straight years in the world top-100.
extra: Pour: a bartender-guided mezcal flight — smoke, wet earth, minerality — Oaxaca by way of Athens.

old.name: Heteroclito
old.label: SINCE 2012
old.teaser: Athens' natural-wine incubator since 2012 — a Greek-only list that poured growers before they had distributors.
old.text: Widely credited as the centre's first dedicated natural-wine cave, opened in 2012 by Madeleine Lorantou and Dimitris Koumanis in a tiny 1957 corner room behind the Metropolitan Cathedral. Before Greek natural wine had importers, this is where it was poured: an all-Greek list of around 200 labels, roughly four-fifths low-intervention, some twenty of them by the glass on a monthly rotation, with growers like Kalathas, Ligas and Tetramythos building their Athens audience here before they had distributors. Barely a chair inside — most people drink standing on the Fokionos lane, cathedral bells behind, over Greek cheese-and-charcuterie boards and Eastern-Mediterranean plates from the Feyrouz family.
extra: Pour: a cloudy Tinos white from Domaine de Kalathas — Jérôme Binda's saline, orchard-wild island wine; then carry a bottle back to the boat at cave price.

old.name: Tanini Agapi Mou
old.label: ~90 BY THE GLASS
old.teaser: The city's deepest all-Greek natural pour — about 90 of its ~100 biodynamic labels open by the glass.
old.text: The name means 'tannin, my love', and the room delivers the city's deepest all-Greek natural pour: of roughly a hundred organic and biodynamic labels, about ninety are open by the glass. Opened December 2018 on Exarchia's quieter Neapoli edge — plants draping from the ceiling, birchwood tables from independent makers, staff in no uniform — it earned Culinary Backstreets' title of 'the people's wine bar' in 2023, chef Maria Kofitsa building the small plates around whatever is in your glass. A Greek-only cellar: if the night demands Jura or the Loire, this is not the room.
extra: Pour: Sotiris Koutroulis's skin-contact Malagousia — an Attica orange wine, apricot skin, dried herb, gentle amber grip.

bars:Alexander's Bar.group: The grand hotels and the one roof

old.name: Alexander's Bar
old.label: SINCE 1874
old.teaser: The most civilized indoor drink in Athens — a stirred classic under an 18th-century Alexander tapestry beats every rooftop on a windy night.
old.text: On the ground floor of the Grande Bretagne, facing Parliament: wood, leather, a walk-in cigar humidor next door, and above the bar an authentic 18th-century tapestry of Alexander victorious at Gaugamela. The hotel was founded in 1874 by Efstathios Lampsas, a peasant-born palace cook who bought Athens' grandest address on an 800,000-drachma loan; the building was Greek GHQ, then Nazi and then British headquarters through the war, and at Christmas 1944 EAM partisans — Manolis Glezos among them — packed its sewers with dynamite, then called the operation off on learning Winston Churchill had just checked in. No view and no terrace: on a windy night this room and one of the city's deepest brandy cellars beat every rooftop in Athens.
extra: Pour: a Negroni, or a warm-bowled old cognac from the brandy list — then a cigar chosen next door in Alexander's humidor.

bars:The Line bars at the Athenaeum Inte.group: The grand hotels and the one roof

old.name: The Line bars at the Athenaeum InterContinental
old.label: LIST BY LINE
old.teaser: The one grand-hotel bar outside the Grande Bretagne worth crossing town for — Europe's No.1 bar team writing the list for a piano lounge and an Acropolis-view rooftop.
old.text: Athens' bar renaissance has climbed into the grand hotels. The team behind Line — Europe's No.1 bar of 2026, the ferment-everything ex-gallery in Kato Petralona — writes the cocktail lists here under a three-year collaboration built around its world ranking, drinks 'inspired by the hotel's art collection' poured across the lobby Artlounge, the retro ToBar and the rooftop Première with its Acropolis line of sight, on Syngrou in Neos Kosmos. A live piano works the Artlounge on winter evenings; the rooftop opens in the warm months. Not a wood-and-leather heritage room and not on the tourist-rooftop trail — a large hotel on a busy avenue whose reason to visit is who makes the drinks: the grand hotels no longer set the bar, they hire it.
extra: Pour: a Line-built 'art-collection' cocktail from its fruit-wine and ferment repertoire — in the Artlounge, or up on the Première rooftop with the Acropolis floodlit.

bars:A for Athens.group: The grand hotels and the one roof

old.name: A for Athens
old.label: ACROPOLIS VIEW
old.teaser: Order one drink for the centre's best straight-on Acropolis sightline — then go drink where the bartenders are.
old.text: The top-floor, two-level roof of a small design hotel on scruffy Miaouli street became the postcard of Athens' 2010s bar awakening: a UNESCO monument straight ahead, a cocktail list themed on love, hope and realism. The scene's centre of gravity has since moved down to street level and out to Petralona, and this is no longer a bartender's bar — the drinks run second to the view. Blue hour, when the floodlights come up over Monastiraki Square, is the whole reason to ride the lift; skip it on a hazy or windy day.
extra: Pour: 'Open Your Eyes' — gin with ratatouille ketchup and tomato vermouth — savoury, drunk against the floodlit Parthenon.

Labels: In the glass · On the label · Ask for. No Maps.

old.name: Markos Vamvakaris — the Patriarch of the bouzouki
old.teaser: A teenage stowaway from Syros swore to sever his own hand if he couldn't learn the bouzouki in six months — and kept both the vow and the hand.
old.text: Rebetiko — the Greek urban blues — took its classic form after the 1922 Asia Minor refugee influx; that portside origin now has its own Piraeus guide . Markos Vamvakaris (1905–1972) left Syros at about twelve and worked bottom-up — stevedore, coal-lugger, the abattoirs — where he made the vow, and kept the hand. He cut his first discs in 1932 ('Efoumernam' ena vrady'), and around 1934 formed the first bouzouki ensemble to record and tour, with Batis, Delias and Pagioumtzis — moving the music out of the teke and onto shellac. His 1935 'Frangosyriani,' a love song to a Catholic girl of Syros, found mass fame only some twenty-five years later, in the early-1960s revival. Every kompania in Athens still opens on Markos: the ground floor of the whole building.

old.name: Tsitsanis — 'Synnefiasmeni Kyriaki,' the occupation's song
old.teaser: Greece's most-loved song was composed in 1943 under the German occupation — and could only reach a record five years later, in 1948.
old.text: Vasilis Tsitsanis (1915–1984) wrote 'Synnefiasmeni Kyriaki' (Cloudy Sunday) in 1943–44 in occupied Thessaloniki, in the shadow of the Great Famine — 'the melody came out of the cloudy occupation,' he said. With the studios shut through the war it reached shellac only in 1948, sung by Prodromos Tsaousakis with Sotiria Bellou; Stelios Kazantzidis cut the celebrated version in 1959. It is the one song an entire taverna will still sing unprompted — and Tsitsanis is the bridge figure who lifted rebetiko toward the mainstream without breaking it.

old.name: 1960: the entechno bridge — a bouzouki at the Academy Awards
old.teaser: In one year, 1960, Athens' two great composers carried the bouzouki from the hash den to the Academy Awards, and founded national art music.
old.text: Manos Hadjidakis wrote the theme for Melina Mercouri in Jules Dassin's 'Never on Sunday' (1960); at the 33rd Academy Awards, on 17 April 1961, it took Best Original Song — the first winner from a foreign-language film; its harbour setting now belongs to the Piraeus guide . The same year Mikis Theodorakis set Yannis Ritsos' 'Epitaphios' (the poem dates to 1936), and two rival recordings appeared within weeks — Hadjidakis's refined orchestration sung by Nana Mouskouri, and Theodorakis's laiko version, Grigoris Bithikotsis over Manolis Chiotis' bouzouki. The Bithikotsis reading founded entechno outright: the exact moment rebetiko's instrument became national art music.

old.name: The rooms — and when they go dark
old.teaser: Half the rebetiko circuit is unlit from June to September, so the honest July promise is short — and it points at daylight.
old.text: Kapnikarea (Christopoulou 2 & Ermou 57) is the surest bet: an Ikarian tailor, Sotiris Sofos, put tables in a Byzantine church's shadow in 1977, and since Ermou went pedestrian in 1996 his son Dimitris has let a rotating pool of some twenty-five musicians work the alley most afternoons from about 14:30 — unamplified rebetiko at table height, year-round, a small per-head music charge, no stage, no setlist. Taverna Klimataria (Plateia Theatrou 2, since 1927) is the other room that plays through the year, live music Tuesday to Sunday. The storied winter rooms go dark June to September: Giorgos Xintaris's Friday residency at Mousiki Skini Hamam in Ano Petralona runs October to May, and the Varvakios arcade's Stoa Athanaton on Sofokleous 17–19 still sings in 2026 — but under a shifting name, so it is a phone call, not a promise. For a July night, take the daylight kompania at Kapnikarea and let the winter rooms wait for winter.

listening:Half Note Jazz Club.group: Jazz, vinyl and the listening room

old.name: The modern clock — a Mets jazz cellar and an analog prophet
old.teaser: Today's Athens runs on two currents: a forty-year-old jazz club in Mets the whole scene orbits, and a 1980s synth poet the world's crate-diggers rediscovered on reissue vinyl.
old.text: Half Note Jazz Club (Trivonianou 17, Mets) has been Athens' serious jazz room for over four decades; its 2025–26 season ran Gilad Hekselman and the Stavros Lantsias Octet — but it closes every summer and Easter week, so a July visitor hears jazz instead at the free Athens Jazz festival at Technopolis in late June. The crate-digger thread runs the other way: Lena Platonos cut 'Gallop' in 1985 — analog synths, a TR-808, her own surreal spoken poetry — reissued by San Francisco's Dark Entries in 2015, and she is now the Athenian name international diggers hunt on vinyl.
